dedupe_keys.name: avatiu port development project rarotonga climate proofed port rebuild cook islands adb 2011 2012

description: The rebuild of Avatiu port on Rarotonga, the main international port of the Cook Islands, financed by an Asian Development Bank loan and described in ADB project documents and a 2013 results story. Coverage: Avatiu harbour, which handles about 90 percent of food imports and all fuel supply for the country. Setting and aims: the 1989 wharf was ageing, poorly designed and damaged by cyclones, and the 2007 Infrastructure Master Plan ranked it a high priority because of the risk of catastrophic failure. Works from March 2011 to August 2012, valued at over 20 million dollars, widened the entrance, dredged alongside, enlarged the turning area, rebuilt and realigned the quay and repaired the wharf deck. Outcome: port life extended by 50 years, with the wharf edge designed to be raised 500 mm for forecast sea level rise without strengthening the wall, fuel and gas pits at the berth replacing floating pipelines, and berthing for ships up to 120 m. Format and access: free ADB web pages and PDF reports. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence stated. Caveats: the results story is the bank's own account. Useful as a climate adaptation and capacity planning example for small island ports and fuel import chains. It relates to the Cook Islands infrastructure investment plan and the Manatua cable outage case study in the catalogue.
